issues.legal_issue: Registered lease terms restricting the permitted building and limiting the payment for it on surrender can qualify as stipulations concerning the erection of buildings, displacing the tenant’s statutory rights to compensation and to purchase the land.
material_facts: The tenant leased vacant land under a written, registered lease and constructed a building after entering the lease.
The lease limited the building’s cost, required the landlord’s approval of its plan, and required construction in accordance with the approved plan.
The lease required the tenant to surrender the land and building at the end of the lease in exchange for a contractually limited payment for the building.
After the landlord brought an ejectment suit, the tenant resisted surrender and applied to have the landlord directed to sell the land.
issues.conclusion: The building restrictions, read with the term limiting payment for the building, were stipulations concerning the erection of buildings covered by the proviso to section 12. They displaced the tenant’s right to compensation under section 3, so the tenant could not claim the purchase option under section 9. The appeal was allowed and the landlord’s claim for possession was restored subject to the conditions set by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 generally protects a tenant’s rights under the Act from contractual deprivation or limitation, but its proviso preserves stipulations made in writing and registered concerning the erection of buildings constructed after the contract. Sections 3 and 9 operate subject to that proviso: a tenant must be entitled to compensation under section 3 to seek the purchase option under section 9. In Vajrapani Naidu v. New Theatre Carnatic Talkies, [1964] 6 S.C.R. 1015, a term requiring demolition and surrender of vacant land was held not to be a stipulation concerning the erection of buildings; the examples of building restrictions given there were illustrative, not exhaustive. V. S. Mudaliar v. N. A. Raghava Chary, [1969] 2 S.C.R. 158, held that a registered stipulation restricting construction so as to prevent a claim for the building’s value could override the right to compensation and, consequently, the purchase option. R. V. Naidu v. Naraindas, [1966] 1 S.C.R. 110, concerned an unregistered lease, so the proviso did not apply. Section 13 addresses the displacement or modification of the Transfer of Property Act to the extent necessary to give effect to the Act.

rule.if: ejectment_suit_with_purchase_application and registered_lease_building_restrictions and post_contract_building and limited_contractual_building_payment

predicates.ejectment_suit_with_purchase_application: A landlord brought an ejectment suit, and the tenant applied to require the landlord to sell the leased land.
predicates.registered_lease_building_restrictions: The tenant made a written, registered agreement restricting the building’s cost or requiring approval of its plan and compliance with that plan.
predicates.post_contract_building: The tenant constructed the building after making the agreement.
predicates.limited_contractual_building_payment: The agreement limited the payment the landlord would make for the building when the tenant surrendered the land.

issues.definition: When an ejectment suit and purchase application involve a building erected after a registered lease that restricts its construction and limits payment for it, the tenant cannot claim statutory compensation or the purchase option.
